question: Which of the following statements regarding hydrogen halides HF, HCL, HBr, HI is correct ?:

options.opa: In aqueous solution they have an acid character and their acid strength increases according to HF <HCI <HBr <HI.
options.opb: In all of them there are intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
options.opc: They are all liquid under normal pressure and temperature conditions.
options.opd: They are obtained by oxidation of the corresponding halogen.

analysis: Hydrogen halides HF, HCL, HBr, HI have an acid character in aqueous solution, with their acid strength increasing according to HI > HBr > HCl > HF. They do not all have intermolecular hydrogen bonds, and they are not all liquid under normal conditions. They are not obtained by oxidation of the corresponding halogen.
